title: dockato: no second rotation / one-sided second rotation
purpose: `dockato` [@epsrmanual] builds larger molecules from `.ato` building blocks: copies of the first molecule of a docking file are bonded onto free sites of a docked file, removing one atom of each to form the new bond. This case covers the branches without a dihedral reference atom on one or both molecules.
fortran: `dockato.f`: `dockato` (driver, parameters from command line or stdin), `rotatem`, `random_rotatem`, `search_unsaturated`, `find_valence`
system: The building block `WaterMolecule.ato` of EPSR-test: one water molecule (O1, H1, H1; O-H 0.976 Å, H-H 1.54 Å, SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charges [@berendsen1987]) in a 14.42 Å box at 300 K. Atom `atomd` of the new molecule is placed on `atomv`, the molecule is rotated so that its `atomdr` neighbour lies on the `atomvr` neighbour of `atomv` (equal bond lengths required), an optional second (dihedral) rotation about the new bond uses `atomdrr`/`atomvrr` (random angle in [dminrr, dmaxrr] from `ran1`, the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992], or a fixed dihedral that creates a DIH group when dminrr = dmaxrr), overlaps are tested with a distance factor, `atomd` and `atomvr` are removed and the new rotational group, bonds and atom types are updated. Water units are again joined by O-O bonds.
inputs: Command line only. Run 1: atomdrr = atomvrr = `0`, angles 0 0, `nooverlaps` (factor 1.0), 3 molecules (`waternorot`); run 2: atomvrr = 0 only, angle range 10-170°, factor 1.0, 3 molecules (`waterhalf`).
verification: Each run writes one new `.ato` file (coordinates, bonds, rotational groups, atom types and the random-number state), compared byte for byte with the stored Fortran output. Run 1: no second rotation; since dminrr = dmaxrr DIH groups are still created (2 DIH groups in `waternorot.ato`). Run 2: the docking molecule is rotated by the random angle itself (2 ROT groups in `waterhalf.ato`). Both outputs hold 5 atoms (2 of the 3 requested dockings).
notes: Fortran behaviour reproduced: the DIH groups of run 1 get the atom pair (0,0) because the Fortran reads `nbond(0)`, the preceding COMMON element, which is 0.
